newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Electrolux goes full steam into Asia.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux goes full steam into Asia.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker AB Electrolux is gearing up investments in Asia in the hope of becoming one of the region's leading suppliers, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
Stefan Schlyter, senior vice president of household appliances in East Asia, said the company had been overly cautious and had underestimated Asia's growth potential.
"Just over a year ago, Electrolux's ambition was to double sales in Asia within three to five years," Schlyter told a news conference launching the new Alpha Care range of products.
"Clearly, we were being too cautious because Electrolux will already achieve our goal of sales exceeding US$1.8 billion by the end of this year," he said.
Sales in Asia for 1995 stood at US$1.0 billion.
Schlyter said that as investment strategies throughout Asia were paying off faster than the company had expected, Electrolux was redefining its goals.

"Our ambition now is for Electrolux to become the market leader throughout the ASEAN region for fully-automated washing machines and vacuum cleaners with a market share of 20 percent in value," Schlyter said, adding the aim was to achieve this by 2000. No dollar equivalent was available.
ASEAN, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
For washing machines and vacuum cleaners, Electrolux holds a 13 percent market share in Thailand, 13-15 percent in Indonesia and 7-8 percent in Malaysia and Singapore, Schlyter said.
He said future sales targets largely depended on sale performances in China, India and Japan.
This year, Japan, together with Thailand, have been the two largest contributors for Electrolux. China was expected to be the biggest market in Asia for the company by 1997.
Electrolux spent about US$10 million in advertising and brand building this year and it intended to spend roughly the same amount or slightly more next year, Schlyter said.
Electrolux has production facilities in China, India, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam.
